Underground Astronauts

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Unveiling the Underground Astronauts: Exploring the Hidden Secrets of Homo naledi

In the depths of remote underground caves, Dr Marina Elliot and Dr Keneiloe Molopayne, the extraordinary "Underground Astronauts," embark on a courageous quest to uncover and study hominid fossils that have remained undisturbed for hundreds of thousands of years. Their groundbreaking discoveries challenge conventional beliefs about our evolutionary journey and shed light on the remarkable species known as Homo naledi.

Among their astonishing findings is evidence suggesting that Homo naledi buried their dead, a practice previously thought to be exclusive to Homo sapiens. Preserved bones found deep within the underground caves offer a haunting glimpse into the ancient rituals of this enigmatic species.Furthermore, the discovery of intentional rock sketches within the cave hints at the possibility that Homo naledi had an artistic side, a revelation that forever changes our perception of their capabilities and behaviours. These extraordinary findings challenge the notion of a linear evolutionary path and instead reveal a complex web of multiple species evolving simultaneously.

By examining Homo naledi, the Underground Astronauts have shattered the long-held belief of a "missing link" in our evolutionary history. Instead, they present a paradigm-shifting idea: the existence of a diverse range of species coexisting and evolving side by side. This revolutionary insight suggests that Homo naledi and Homo sapiens potentially overlapped in time, raising intriguing questions about our shared ancestry.

Perhaps the most astonishing revelation lies in the size of Homo naledi's brain, which is comparable to that of an orange—approximately one-third the size of Homo sapiens. This challenges the preconception that higher intelligence and self-reflection depend solely on brain size. The Underground Astronauts' discoveries demonstrate that Homo naledi possessed a remarkable capacity for self-reflection and awareness of death, despite their relatively small brain size.

Dr Lee Berger is the pioneer who initiated the exploration of the Rising Star cave system and created a team of underground astronauts. Together, they have unearthed a captivating past record, redefining our understanding of human evolution.

Underground Astronauts Script Viewing 2

Early morning sunrise and drone shots.

Dr Kene UPSOUND

“Every single day is a new adventure…”
Lee Berger UPSOUND
“You’re gonna drop about 30m in this journey over about 100m.”
“Not too tight?”
“This is not particular extreme caving but there are parts that are tight”
Link
It’s an early, very chilly morning here at the Cradle of Humankind, and I am with a group of very special people. They are called underground astronauts and are about to enter this Rising Star cave system to try to unlock secrets of our past.
V/O
The discovery of four human ancestors or hominids right here in Gauteng’s Cradle, has played an important role in unravelling the history of human evolution.
Kene
It’s a slow process.. And it’s exciting because you never know what might pop up…
V/O
WITS Paleo anthropologist Dr Keneiloe Molopyane studies human evolution through fossils. She was awarded the prestigious National Geographic title of Emerging Explorer in 2021 and now heads up the team of underground astronauts.
Kene
I always wanted to be an archaeologist since the age of 7. I was just fascinated because there was this idea that you could tell a story from a time long gone and from voices that can no longer speak.


V/O
National Geographic Explorer in Residence and Wits paleo anthropologist Prof Lee Berger is credited with finding two hominids in his career, Australopithecus sediba in 2008, and in 2015 Homo naledi was revealed to the world.


Ladies and Gentlemen, I give you a new species of human ancestor – Homo naledi


V/O

Homo naledi was discovered in The Rising Star cave system, only 2 km from the famous Sterkfontein Caves.

Although cavers have regularly explored its rocky corridors, Naledi’s remains lay undisturbed because they lay in an inaccessible cave below a dangerous twelve metre vertical chute with some gaps only as wide as a pencil.

Some grunting here

V/O
Prof Berger realised he needed help getting into the cave so he advertised for scientists with at least a master's degree, a lean frame, caving experience and the ability to work in extremely claustrophobic spaces.

He watched from his command centre above ground while a band of women explored the extraordinary history of humankind.

Lee
For days and days, we sat watching these images
that would flicker between colours and then go to infrared and black and white.

And it felt like those early images you see from the space programme, you know, there's Apollo images. In the middle of all that. In one of these interviews, I blurted out, you know, they're incredible heroes. They're like astronauts.
But underground astronauts. And it stuck.


UPS Let’s turn this bad boy on. (Masa turns on her headlamp)
We are ready to go. Ready. Hug the wall if you need to hug the wall.


V/O
I have been given the wonderful privilege of accompanying the team.

V/O
Part of the laughter is nervousness… the trip to the burial site is treacherous. It is about ninety metres underground, and there are steep drops and some claustrophobically narrow spaces and a section where you can only fit through if your one arm is held straight in front you - like superman.


Masa
And there I have made it out of Superman’s crawl. And you know what they say. If you make it out Superman’s crawl you are a bit of a superhero.


V/O
And I’ve arrived at Dragon’s back where Dr Molopyane and team are excavating.

Masa
Talk about an exciting job. This is no ordinary 9 to 5.

Keneiloe
Oh, yeah. I'm pretty much a grown adult who's never outgrown her sandbox days. I love playing in the sand. Well, what I do is called excavation. Yeah.

V/O
Puzzling out the past takes years of rigorous scientific research. When Homo naledi was found, all we knew was what their bones told us - they were small, walked upright and had a mixture of ape and human features.

Now ten years later we have a far fuller picture – the bones have been dated to around three hundred thousand years – so they were alive at the same time as humans were.

And last year, Dr Molopyane and her team made the remarkable discovery of fire remnants in this cave.

UPS It looks very distinctively like charcoal to me.

Kene
If you find fire in your site that is big news.

Masa
Right.

Kene
Because either hominids or using fire or you having different individuals using the space and possibly at different times. Some of those small bones that were finding were burnt and some are cracked open. And usually when that happens
at an archeological site, it's a sign of cooking. I'm not saying that that's possibly
what happened here, but it's a possibility.

Masa
And so silly question, we all show that, you know, somebody didn't just come in here, have some chicken wings and leave some bones.

Kene
It's actually a question I asked myself last year. I'm like, hold on, it's easy for me to get in here. Right? But let's be fair. You wouldn't come down to this pad for funsies. That's right. So the likelihood of someone just coming in here having a picnic on the ground is unlikely.

V/O
In the cave without my headlamp the darkness is oppressive. It makes logical sense that Homo naledi must have used fire to navigate their way around here.

Masa
Prof Berger, I must tell you that I am having a lot of fun down here; it’s a beautiful space as well. What are we looking for?

Lee
So we are in now the passages that Homo naledi would have used to actually reach places like Dragon’s back and Dinaledi.

So maybe a quarter of a million years ago you can imagine they would have been coming down these long passages. Then some of them would perhaps climb that steep climb and then descend down that steep shoot up and descend into Dinaledi carrying a body.

Masa
How do we know this?

Prof Berger
Because we have burials in the Dinaledi chamber. Children and adults,
holes dug in the ground with curled up bodies and
then covered by the dirt from the hole. And what's remarkable about that
is the thing we're describing, which you could understand
if it were a human to human thing, it wasn't done by a human.

Link
Right back here is the Dinaledi chamber, only 47 people have ever ventured into these parts, more people have gone out into space. But unfortunately I will not be allowed this point today but what a treat to come this close.

V/O
As one of those 47, Dr Molopyane has discovered many fossils in the burial chamber.

Masa
What does that feel like for you Doc when you make such a discovery and you unearth such things.

Kene
That is the most incredible feeling. It is so exciting. You could cry sometimes.

V/O
Before calling it a day at the cave I decided to try my hand at a little archaeology…
•
Masa
I found something…
•
Sarah
So this one is a rock
•
Masa
Have I found something
Sarah
More rock
•
Masa
Can we now call me an underground astronaut.
•
Laughing

V/O
This dedicated team’s research shows a species with a brain only a third the size of ours, but one that consciously buried it's dead – 100 000 years before we did.

Unusual engravings on the dolomite cave walls were also discovered in the burial chamber, and one wonders whether these symbols were made by them?


Lee
Until recently we only knew about it’s anatomy because that is all we had. Now we know that it is also a cultural species.

Masa
That’s a game changer.

Lee
I think it is. I think it’s undeniable. No matter how you interpret what we are putting out now, it’s clear that they are doing something profoundly more than just living as apes on a landscape.



Teasers

Teaser 1
VIZ & UPS:

VO: Only a select few have been into space and even fewer have been into the Rising Star cave in Gauteng with the richest discovery of human ancestor bones in the world.

UPS: Every single day is an adventure

VO: A team of underground astronauts has unearthed the bones of Homo naledi – a species that has revolutionised our perceptions of ancient minds.


Teaser 2
VIZ & UPS:
VO: To boldly go where no man has gone before – this is the mission of the underground astronauts.

UPS: Lee: I grew up in an age in this field when everyone said that there was nothing left to find. And it’s not true, and we are living in this greatest age of exploration.

VO: Who are these specialists who unearthed the hominid Homo naledi… and are now discovering the path of evolution, one bone at a time.

Teaser 3

VO
Humans were not the first species to bury their dead. Homo naledi – a new member of our ancestor family — deliberately buried loved ones in an obscure cave one hundred thousand years before we did.

Lee
It’s clear that they are doing something profoundly more than just living as apes on a landscape.
